page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes a 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded performance but limited multi-threaded scaling due to the single physical core configuration. Single-core stress-ng performance and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, rank in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require predictable single-thread performance without massive parallel processing needs. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic utility tasks. However, it is less optimal for highly parallelized workloads, database operations, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, where multi-core performance and memory bandwidth constraints become bottlenecks.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-threaded CPU performance and compression speeds, alongside average memory bandwidth for large blocks. However, its multi-core performance, database operations, and software compilation capabilities are relatively weak due to the single physical core limitation.
